summary.intent: Squash 38 messy iterative commits (attach command implementation, fixes, lint, review feedback) down to a clean 4-commit history rebased onto origin/main.
summary.outcome: Successfully produced 4 clean commits with diff checksum verified identical to the original PR, all tests passing and zero lint issues.

repo: The repo uses an 'entire' CLI tool with a cmd/entire/cli/ structure for attach-related commands.

Commit history included distinct layers: initial implementation, gemini fix, simplify+lint, and copilot review feedback — all ultimately collapsed into a single attach commit plus a review-feedback commit.

code.finding: Main attach command implementation — underwent iterative fixes including a Gemini-specific fix and review feedback (trailer heuristic tightening, lint, refactoring).
Test file for attach command; all tests passed after the rebase.

workflow: Diff checksum (e541bd8b) was used to verify the squashed history is byte-for-byte identical to the original PR diff — a reliable sanity check after interactive rebase.
Keeping a backup branch (attach-session-id-backup) before destructive rebase operations is standard practice here.
Iterative fix commits (gemini fix, simplify) that lack meaning without their parent implementation should be folded into the parent commit rather than kept separate.
Lint and full test suite were run as final verification after rebase to confirm no regressions.

friction: Determining which commits to fold together required careful inspection of the commit graph — the gemini fix and simplify commits sat between the initial implementation and review feedback, making the grouping non-obvious.
Multiple intermediate verification steps (checksum, file count, insertion/deletion stats) were needed to build confidence the rebase hadn't silently altered the diff.
open_items: Backup branch 'attach-session-id-backup' still exists and should be deleted once the PR is merged.
The rebased branch has not been pushed — a force-push to the remote PR branch is still pending.
